newsitem.title: UK: Burton shares fall, hit by poor sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Burton shares fall, hit by poor sentiment.

text.p: Shares in clothing retailer Burton Group Plc slipped on Thursday after group profits did no more than meet average expectations.
The shares were among the day's most active, falling 6-1/2p to 147-1/2p in trade of 6.6 million shares by 0850 GMT.
Burton reported pretax profits of 108.1 million stg, up 22.7 percent from last year and in the middle of the range of analysts expectations.
A dividend of 1.4 pence topped most analysts forecasts.
Elsewhere, the company reported an 11-percent increase in second half sales in the first ten weeks and said gross margins were up by 0.7 pct.
But traders said the shares had been bought in the run-up to the results on expectations of a strong recovery, leaving some investors disappointed.
Over the last month, shares in Burton have risen four percent.
"People had been pushing Burton as a recovery stock but the results don't really show that the recovery is racing ahead and so they're turning a bit cautious," one dealer said.
Since the beginning of the year the sector has been dogged by poor sentiment. Burton underperformed the rest of its sector by 22 percent and the FTSE-All Shares index by 11 percent since January.
"The results were virtually in line with forecasts," another dealer said. "But sentiment has turned after they had a bit of a run up before the figures."
